description: We are Vison Coders_369, a team of passionate students interested in space science, technology, innovation, and problem-solving. We aim to develop creative and impactful solutions for real-world challenges through NASA Space Apps Challenge.
summary:
"VISION ASTRAA" is an interactive planetary intelligence and digital twin platform designed to identify Earth locations with terrain characteristics similar to selected regions on the Moon and Mars.

Planetary exploration requires understanding unfamiliar landscapes, but comparing terrain datasets across different celestial bodies is challenging because of variations in resolution, coordinate systems, and data formats.

Our platform addresses this problem by integrating planetary terrain data into a unified analytical environment. It uses digital elevation models, terrain slope, ruggedness, relative relief, and other environmental indicators to compare planetary regions with potential Earth analogues.

VISION ASTRAA combines interactive 3D planetary exploration, geospatial analysis, weighted similarity scoring, and visual dashboards to make complex terrain comparisons easier to understand.

By connecting planetary science with accessible visual technology, our solution aims to support scientific research, analogue mission planning, and STEM education.

Our vision is to make planetary exploration more accessible, data-driven, and collaborative while helping researchers and students better understand the landscapes of other worlds.
details:
VISION ASTRAA

Earth–Moon–Mars Terrain Intelligence & Digital Twin Platform

1. Project Overview

VISION ASTRAA is an interactive planetary intelligence and digital twin platform developed by Team Vision Coders_369 to address the NASA Space Apps Challenge: “Identify Earth Locations that Analog the Permanent Moon Base Locations and Mars.”

Our project bridges the gap between planetary exploration and terrestrial research by helping users identify Earth locations that share geological, topographical, and environmental characteristics with selected regions on the Moon and Mars.

Planetary datasets are often distributed across different sources, formats, resolutions, and coordinate reference systems. Comparing these datasets manually requires specialised knowledge and sophisticated geospatial tools.

VISION ASTRAA aims to simplify this process through an integrated platform that combines planetary visualisation, terrain analysis, Earth analogue discovery, and explainable similarity scoring.

2. How Our Project Works

VISION ASTRAA follows a structured workflow to analyse planetary terrain and identify potential Earth analogues.

Step 1 — Planetary Exploration

Users can explore interactive 3D representations of Earth, the Moon, and Mars, select regions of interest, and inspect geographical and terrain characteristics.

Step 2 — Data Acquisition and Processing

The platform is designed to work with planetary and terrestrial datasets, including digital elevation models (DEMs) and geospatial information.

Relevant datasets are prepared through preprocessing, coordinate alignment, resolution standardisation, and numerical normalisation to support cross-planetary comparisons.

Step 3 — Terrain Feature Extraction

The system analyses terrain characteristics such as:

  • Surface elevation and local elevation variation.
  • Mean surface slope.
  • Terrain ruggedness.
  • Relative topographic relief.
  • Thermal characteristics.
  • Water and ice indicators, where supported by available data.

These parameters help describe the physical similarities and differences between planetary environments.

Step 4 — Earth Analogue Identification

VISION ASTRAA compares selected lunar or Martian regions against candidate Earth locations using a weighted similarity model.

The system evaluates individual terrain features, calculates similarity scores, and ranks potential Earth analogues.

Users can examine feature-level comparisons to understand why a particular terrestrial location received its score.

Step 5 — Interactive Results and Visualisation

The platform presents its analytical outputs through interactive dashboards, terrain comparisons, charts, maps, and 3D visualisations.

This enables users to interpret complex geospatial information more easily and investigate potential analogue locations.

3. Key Features and Innovations

Interactive Planetary Explorer: Explore Earth, Moon, and Mars through interactive planetary visualisations.

Earth Analogue Finder: Identify candidate terrestrial locations resembling selected lunar and Martian environments.

Terrain Comparison Studio: Compare planetary terrain characteristics through a unified interface.

Morphometric Analysis: Examine slope, ruggedness, elevation variation, and relative relief.

Explainable Similarity Scoring: View weighted similarity results and individual feature contributions rather than relying only on a single matching percentage.

Scientific Visualisation: Interpret results using graphical dashboards, charts, maps, and comparative terrain views.

Research-Oriented Interface: Bring planetary exploration and terrain analysis together in an accessible web-based environment.

A key creative aspect of VISION ASTRAA is its integration of planetary exploration, quantitative terrain comparison, and Earth analogue discovery into a single interactive experience.

4. Technologies and Tools Used

Our project uses a combination of web development, geospatial processing, numerical analysis, and scientific visualisation technologies.

Programming Languages

  • Python
  • TypeScript

Geospatial and Scientific Processing

  • GDAL / Rasterio
  • NumPy
  • SciPy
  • Scikit-learn

Visualisation and Mapping

  • CesiumJS
  • Leaflet
  • Interactive web dashboards
  • 2D and 3D terrain visualisation

Data Resources

  • NASA Earthdata
  • NASA Planetary Data System (PDS)
  • NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) resources
  • Digital elevation models and other relevant geospatial datasets

System Architecture

The proposed architecture connects data acquisition, preprocessing, terrain feature extraction, similarity analysis, and interactive visualisation through a web-based interface.

The platform is designed to support further integration of scientific datasets and analytical capabilities.

5. Benefits and Intended Impact

VISION ASTRAA aims to make planetary terrain analysis more accessible, understandable, and useful.

Supporting Planetary Research

Researchers can use terrain comparisons to identify potential Earth analogue sites for further scientific investigation.

Assisting Analogue Mission Planning

Earth locations with relevant terrain characteristics may help researchers investigate operational challenges associated with planetary exploration.

Improving STEM Education

Students can explore planetary environments, compare terrain characteristics, and understand geospatial analysis through interactive visualisations.

Reducing Technical Barriers

A unified interface can reduce the need to switch between multiple specialised applications for basic exploration and comparison tasks.

Encouraging Scientific Collaboration

The platform provides a foundation for future collaboration among students, researchers, educators, and planetary science communities.

6. Challenges and Design Considerations

During development, our team considered several important scientific and technical challenges.

Dataset Compatibility: Earth, Moon, and Mars datasets may use different coordinate systems, spatial resolutions, measurement units, and elevation reference datums.

Scientific Comparability: Directly comparing absolute elevations across planetary bodies can be misleading. Relative terrain characteristics provide a more meaningful basis for some comparisons.

Feature Weighting: Different terrain characteristics may have different levels of importance depending on the intended scientific application.

Data Availability: Some planetary regions have limited coverage or incomplete environmental information.

Interpretability: Similarity results should be accompanied by feature-level explanations so users can understand the basis of a suggested match.

Scientific Limitations: Terrain similarity alone does not establish that an Earth location fully reproduces lunar or Martian conditions. Gravity, atmospheric pressure, radiation, geology, and other environmental factors must also be considered.

Our approach therefore treats similarity scores as comparative analytical indicators rather than definitive measurements of planetary equivalence.

7. Future Scope

Our long-term vision is to develop VISION ASTRAA into a more comprehensive planetary intelligence platform.

Potential future developments include:

  • Integration of additional planetary datasets.
  • Improved terrain classification and similarity models.
  • Expanded catalogues of Earth analogue locations.
  • Advanced 3D terrain reconstruction.
  • Additional environmental and geological comparison parameters.
  • Greater support for scientific reporting and data export.
  • Collaboration features for educational and research institutions.
  • Validation of candidate analogue sites against published scientific research.

8. Conclusion

VISION ASTRAA represents our attempt to make planetary terrain intelligence more accessible through the combination of geospatial science, interactive visualisation, and explainable analytical methods.

By connecting the landscapes of Earth, the Moon, and Mars within a unified platform, our project helps users investigate where terrestrial environments may resemble extraterrestrial terrain.

Our goal is simple: Explore worlds, discover analogues, and advance planetary exploration.
